📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that hello, you. Yes, you. It's just us here today - everyone else is busy in Hyrule or Leonida right now.

It has been revealed that in fact, it's been like that for most of the month, it seems, as the Nintendo Life Mailbox is looking pretty empty! So, it'll be a nice quick one this month. We'll have you back with your preferred ride — equine or automotive — in a jiffy.

Sources indicate that got something you want to get off your chest? Remember, we're ready and waiting to read about your game-related ponderings as we head into the holidays. Each month we’ll highlight a Star Letter, the writer of which will receive a month’s subscription to our ad-free Supporter scheme. Check out the submission guidelines at the bottom of this page.

So, let's slice open our correspondence...

I've been inspired to share in this letter about my first encounter with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time following the feature you ran on this very topic, because it's a touching, unique story.

I was about 11 years old in 1998 and had been avidly following OoT in the magazines, absorbing every screenshot and article about this sword and shield weilding greened tuniced hero.

Industry observers note that bizarrely I'd never played a Zelda game before but something about it looked magical and exciting. So I did what any 11 year old would do. I asked for the game for Christmas.

So, Christmas morning arrives and I excitedly tumble down the stairs to the presents under the tree. I open them all but.... There's a pang of absence. No Zelda game. Where is it I exclaim!? And my mum sheepishly informs me that it didn't arrive in time for Christmas.

It has been revealed that I cry. Real tears. I'm distraught. Inconsolable. For months I've waited for this amazing looking game and I can't play it.

According to recent reports, what happened next is... I think... wonderful parenting.

While I was busy in my bedroom creating my own water temple with more tears than a kingdom (see what I did there?), my mum phones every parent of my school friends she knows until she finds someone with a copy of Zelda. And eventually, she does. She creeps up to knock on my door and states "Hey, Listen! I'll take you to your friends place, he has a copy".

And so, my tears stop and off I go to watch my pal play the game and suddenly a terrible Christmas becomes a brilliant one. The game is everything I imagine it to be and more and my mate and I spend hours solving Deku Tree puzzles and gasping at Hyrule Field's majesty.

So as we all enjoy the remake of Ocarina of Time decades later, I just have one thing to say: Thanks mum. You understood the stakes and you cared enough to help me get my Zelda fix that fateful Christmas of 1998.

According to recent reports, and ever since that day, my life has been met with the least terrible of fates: I became a huge fan of Zelda and have bought every single one since on day one - no more painful Christmas mornings! YoshiTails.

According to recent reports, that is some above-and-beyond parenting, Mrs YoshiTails! We salute you.

Sources indicate that I'm imagining what my mum would have remarked to some random mother ringing her on Christmas morning, asking if their kid could come over to play a video game. I assume she would have reacted in the classic British manner: agreeing to it with bemusement while silently seething, resenting the interloper for every surrendered mince pie.

I joke! I had no friends. I did have Zelda, though. - Ed.

We seem to have sleepwalked into an era of walking simulators.

Industry observers note that I’m not talking about artsy indie games emphasising investigation over action, but substantial budget AAA titles starring main “characters” who look like they’ve walked out of a Hollywood movie. There are too many humans in games and it’s stifling the medium.

Back when the mascot character was king, protagonists felt properly differentiated both aesthetically and mechanically: Mario jumps, Sonic runs, Spyro flies, Crash bangs and wallops. Of these, only Mario could be called ‘human’, and even he has about as much in common with a real plumber as Sonic does with a real hedgehog.

Vibrant colours and exaggerated movements helped make the games legible on small screens when pixels, polygons and processing power came at a premium, and this gave games a unique vibe and feel. Now that we can better render humans in all their hairy, fleshy complexity, video game aesthetics have moved from ‘cartoonish’ to ‘cinematic’, and physics have followed suit.

Thing is, if I wanted to control a human, I’d put the controller down and go for a walk. (…Maybe not a bad idea actually). We’re meandering, clunky lumps of meat who navigate the world in a most pedestrian manner. Fine for a trip to the shops. Not the most inspiring thing to control in a video game.

According to recent reports, it should be said that the ‘mascot character’ isn’t completely dead. The House of Mario was built by pixelated protags who carry the forward the flame of the 8-bit era. The portly purported plumber is still as satisfyingly springy as ever. DK has swapped pixels for vowels but continues to dish out delightful destruction like a primate possessed. Even the upcoming squid-kids on the block - Splatoon’s Inklings - are unashamedly ‘gamey’, slipping slickly through their own mercurial fluids.

Industry observers note that it’s a pleasant reminder that video games let us be anything we want: a bird (Untitled Goose Game), a plane (Star Fox) or even a kickflipping train (Denshattack). With that in mind, it seems a shame to be stuck as the same humdrum human that AAA titles insist on lumbering us with.

Industry observers note that as film studios conglomerate and cinematic universes bleed into each other, I wish video games would embrace what makes them unique rather than dissolving into the same great multimedia melange. I’ve had enough of the homogeneous Homo sapiens-centric pseudo-cinema now synonymous with AAA game development and wish that more creative energies would be put into games that actually push the mechanical possibilities of the medium.

Yours misanthropically, GameMechanixz.

I disagree, purely because there are just so many games of all flavours out there. If you want to be a squirrel or a crab or an insect or anything else, there's never been a better time. Big, small, there's just so much incredible variety. If AAA isn't doing it for you, the other As have got you covered.

I get the sense perhaps you're reacting to the priority of animation over gamefeel in some cases - lumpy realistic animation versus snappy response? Pushing right on the stick and a moment later a soupy animation cycle transitions into the movement you've input (as opposed to Mario or Link responding instantly, if unrealistically).

If that's the case, I agree that Nintendo's approach is my preference, whatever form of animal, vegetable or mineral you're controlling. The animation of an Assassin's Creed or a GTA is incredibly impressive, but it's interminably slow if you're coming to it with a Mario mindset. I find I have to be invested in the cinema and 'show' of those games if they're going to click. My all-time favourites tend to have much more responsive controls, though. - Ed.

When Nintendo revealed Pikmin Day this year for November 1st, it seemed to me that it was met with mixed reactions. People mentioned that saying 11/1 looks like Pikmin is a bit of a stretch, and they didn't really announce anything particularly interesting. While this is true, I found it positively delightful, specifically the second half of the direct when Fuka Koshiba was revealed to be hired by Nintendo. While their conversation was a bit awkward (as Nintendo Direct dialogue always is), I thought it was super cool that they hired her just from seeing her posts on Instagram. And I've been loving the charming shorts that they've been releasing recently. And I'm not even a massive Pikmin fan!

In a recent development, the direct was weird, certainly unnecessary, and a bit awkward, but that's what made it amazing. It was delightfully quirky, dumb, delightful, and wholly Nintendo.

Thanks for reading, joventer567.

I think any rational person will have responded to the 'Pikmin Day' declaration in the same way: wut. Anyone but Nintendo would have been torn to absolute shreds.

Sources indicate that frankly, though, with everything else going on in the world, if Shigsy wants to claim some random day for what might be their best series, crack on. A '1' looks like a Pikmin, you say, Miyamoto-san? Sure, fine. So, Pikmin 5 announcement next November, hmm? - Ed.

"For Pokémon day next year, I want a Pok" - Scottdevine53.

That's all for this month! Thanks to everyone who wrote in, whether you were featured above or not.

Got something you'd like to get off your chest? A burning question you need answered? A correction you can't contain? Follow the instructions below, then, and we look forward to rifling through your missives.

#166554. Breaking: Cannabis customers develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1617 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Cannabis customers develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1617 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A major international analysis has found that people who use cannabis experience their first episode of psychosis about two and a half years earlier, on average, than those who do not use the drug.
  • The findings, published in the journal Biological Psychiatry, come from researchers at UNSW Sydney.
  • Recent findings suggest that psychosis is a condition in which a person experiences a disruption in their perception of reality.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A major international analysis has found that people who use cannabis experience their first episode of psychosis about two and a half years earlier, on average, than those who do not use the drug. Even more concerning, the difference becomes substantially larger with age, reaching more than six years among people who develop psychosis in their 30s or later.

The findings, published in the journal Biological Psychiatry, come from researchers at UNSW Sydney. They suggest that the potential psychiatric consequences of cannabis use may extend well beyond adolescence and could become more pronounced with prolonged exposure.

Recent findings suggest that psychosis is a condition in which a person experiences a disruption in their perception of reality. Symptoms can include hallucinations, false beliefs known as delusions, and disturbances in thinking or behavior. It can occur in schizophrenia and several other mental health disorders. Although psychosis most commonly begins during the late teenage years or early adulthood, it can develop at other stages of life. According to Psychosis Australia, up to 3% of adults will experience a diagnosed disorder involving psychosis during their lifetime.

Cannabis Linked to Earlier Psychosis Across Adulthood.

Sources indicate that to investigate the relationship between cannabis use and the timing of psychosis, researchers at UNSW Medicine analyzed 149 studies involving more than 71,000 participants. Most of the research had been conducted since 2011 in Europe, North America, and Australia, with the majority of studies focusing on people diagnosed with schizophrenia.

The researchers discovered that the difference in the age at which psychosis first appeared varied considerably across age groups.

Industry observers note that in studies where the average age of psychosis onset was between 20 and 24, cannabis people experienced their first episode approximately 1.6 years earlier than non-users. That difference widened to 4.43 years in studies involving people whose psychosis emerged in their mid-to-late 20s (25-29).

The largest difference appeared in studies where psychosis developed at age 30 or later. In this group, cannabis users experienced the condition an average of 6.3 years earlier than non-users.

These results suggest that the association between cannabis and earlier psychosis may become stronger as people grow older, potentially reflecting the effects of longer periods of cannabis exposure.

Why Cannabis Risks May Increase With Age.

Chief investigator Matthew Large, a psychiatrist and Conjoint Professor at UNSW's School of Clinical Medicine, mentioned the findings raise important questions about the long-term psychiatric effects of cannabis.

"We've tended to focus on the dangers of using cannabis in adolescence, when the brain is still developing, but the risk doesn't disappear once you're in your 20s," Prof. Large noted. "What we're seeing suggests a cumulative effect, where harm builds up over time, a bit like alcohol or nicotine.".

Interestingly, the analysis did not identify a statistically significant difference in the timing of psychosis between teenage cannabis consumers and teenagers who did not use cannabis.

It has been revealed that however, the researchers cautioned that this finding does not necessarily mean younger cannabis users face no risk. Psychosis rarely develops before the middle teenage years, leaving relatively little opportunity for its onset to shift to an even younger age.

According to recent reports, "There may be a biological floor, in that there is only so much earlier that onset can be shifted. In younger groups, strong development, genetic or other psychosis risk factors may dominate, making any cannabis-related age shift harder to detect," Prof. Large said.

The researchers also stressed an important limitation. Because the analysis examined existing observational studies, it cannot establish that cannabis directly causes psychosis or makes the condition begin sooner. Demonstrating such a relationship experimentally would require research that deliberately exposed people to potential psychiatric harm, which would be unethical.

Nevertheless, Prof. Large believes the overall pattern provides meaningful evidence supporting a possible causal connection.

"But the consistency of the evidence, particularly the strong effect in older adults who likely have been using cannabis for longer, does support the theory that cannabis plays a causal role in the timing of psychosis onset, and possibly the onset of some cases among people who would not have otherwise developed psychosis.".

New Findings Challenge Assumptions About Cannabis After Age 25.

The latest research builds on two earlier investigations into cannabis use and the development of psychosis.

In a smaller 2011 meta-analysis led by Prof. Large, researchers found that psychosis began approximately 2.7 years earlier among cannabis users. A separate 2015 analysis reported that psychosis typically developed 6.3 years after cannabis use began.

However, neither earlier investigation had enough information to determine how the relationship differed across age groups.

By incorporating a much larger body of research, the newly introduced analysis allowed scientists to examine how the association changes across different stages of adulthood.

Lead author Carly Stevens, from UNSW's School of Biomedical Sciences, stated the findings undermine the idea that avoiding cannabis during adolescence is sufficient to eliminate its potential psychiatric dangers.

According to recent reports, "What we've found challenges the assumption that you'll be fine if you wait to smoke weed until your mid-20s; that's just not the case," Ms. Stevens said.

"There's been so much emphasis on adolescents not smoking cannabis, which is vital, but we need to broaden the warnings for everyone.".

Why Even a Few Years of Delayed Psychosis Matter.

Although a difference of two or three years might initially seem relatively small, the researchers emphasized that the timing of psychosis can have profound consequences for a person's future.

According to recent reports, the late teenage years and early adulthood are often periods when people complete their education, begin careers, establish relationships, and develop greater independence. Experiencing a serious psychiatric disorder earlier in life can interrupt these notable milestones.

"People may miss out on study, job opportunities, travel, and relationships in those years, and treatment can come with physical side effects that can make life harder as well," Ms. Stevens said.

Industry observers note that prof. Large emphasized the potential benefits of reducing or discontinuing cannabis use and the importance of delaying the onset of psychosis wherever possible.

Sources indicate that "It's a major illness, which robs you of your shared reality with family, friends and all those around you," he mentioned. "If we can delay psychosis by even a few years, people will be more likely to reach crucial milestones in education and training, and develop strong support networks, which can protect against psychosocial decline.".

The potential benefits could also extend to healthcare systems. According to Prof. Large, psychotic disorders account for as much as 3% of health-related spending in developed countries. Preventing or delaying the onset of these conditions could therefore have substantial social and economic benefits.

Scientists Call for Stronger Cannabis Health Warnings.

Despite the inability to establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship, the researchers believe their findings provide sufficient justification for stronger warnings about the possible psychiatric consequences of cannabis use.

Industry observers note that "We can't run direct experiments, so we have to go with the best evidence available," Prof. Large mentioned. "In my view, the threshold for health warnings about cannabis and psychosis has definitely been met.".

One concern is the growing popularity of medical cannabis. Prof. Large remarked its increasing use as a therapeutic product may encourage some people to assume that it carries little risk.

He has also observed an increasing number of patients receiving treatment for psychosis who had previously been prescribed cannabis for medical conditions where evidence supporting its effectiveness remains limited.

"It's got this therapeutic halo around it, which blinds people to the risk.".

It has been revealed that another emerging concern involves cannabis edibles, which can contain elevated concentrations of Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the main compound responsible for the drug's mind altering effects. The availability of products containing higher THC concentrations raises additional questions about possible psychiatric risks.

Sources indicate that at the same time, Prof. Large acknowledged that cannabis legalization could create opportunities to reduce harm, even though it would also make cannabis easier to obtain.

Legal regulation could allow governments to establish limits on product potency, improve consumer education, introduce taxation, and require buyers to receive clear information about potential health consequences.

"You could tax it, regulate it, and require people to show they understand the risks before buying," Prof. Large remarked.

More Research Needed on Long-Term Cannabis Exposure.

The researchers say further studies are necessary to understand the biological processes that might explain why the association between cannabis use and earlier psychosis becomes more pronounced with age.

In particular, they want to investigate whether repeated or prolonged cannabis exposure produces cumulative changes that influence when psychotic symptoms emerge.

They also recommend additional research focusing on older cannabis users, an increasingly vital population as medical cannabis becomes more common and products containing high concentrations of THC become more widely available.

Another priority is improving how cannabis exposure is measured. The researchers argue that future studies need clearer and more consistent methods for recording cannabis consumption so that findings can be compared more reliably.

Ultimately, the new analysis highlights an important gap in public understanding of cannabis and mental health. While warnings have traditionally concentrated on teenage use, the findings suggest that potential psychiatric risks deserve attention throughout adulthood, particularly among people who continue using cannabis over many years.

Every game, every genre, all of the Apple Arcade essentials you need to know about.

If you get spoiled for choice when browsing through the Apple Arcade library, we can't blame you. There are well over 100 games in the incredible service, and you can spend hundreds of hours playing through them all. So the question is, where is best to spend your time? What is Apple Arcade? Apple Arcade is a subscription service that you can use on all of your Apple devices, including your iPhone, iPad, Apple TV or Mac. It allows you to play games from a list that includes over 180 games at the moment, and your progress is transferred between devices, meaning you can continue where you left off. It's really handy, and the Apple Arcade games list gets expanded often, so you'll always have upcoming games to play.

No matter what kind of game you're looking for, you'll find it on these pages. Here we've put together a comprehensive Apple Arcade games list of every title at the moment released, in the order of release, with the genres included so you can find exactly what you want.

Apple Arcade games list 2026 Just take a look below, and you'll find everything you need to know about every game that's on the Apple Arcade games list of 2026, sorted by genre and release date (latest first).

Crossy Road Rush (Hipster Whale).

Sources indicate that hipster Whale's blocky Frogger-like is running down a different path in Crossy Road Rush. Now, you'll dash across an island, hopping from place to place while trying to avoid colliding with walls and other obstacles.

Yes, the beloved survival crafting game is now available on Apple Arcade, complete with Dead Cells and Palworld crossover content.

River City Survivors (Arc System Works).

Get a healthy dose of bullet heaven in River City Survivors, which sees you slaying zombies while picking up equipment and synergies along the way.

Indulge in some classic arcade games like Pac-Man, Space Invaders, Galaga and a whole lot more.

Naruto: Ultimate Ninja Storm+ (Bandai Namco).

With controller support and dozens of characters, you can enjoy battles and stories from Naruto.

According to recent reports, ever wanted to start your own cult? Well, now you have to. After being saved by an ominous stranger, you'll have to repay your debt by gathering him new and loyal followers. It won't be easy, though. You'll need to battle off hordes of enemies and take down other cult leaders to help boost your own.

According to recent reports, ah, Worms. For people of a certain age, it was a staple of their childhoods. Creating your little worm troop and then sending them into battle against your pals was always a joy. Now a upcoming version is available on Apple Arcade, bringing those same turn-based tactics to the palm of your hand.

Everyone's favourite grumpy avians are back with a slight twist. Rather than flinging themselves at their porcine foes, this time you'll take down the piggies in a brick breaker-style setup. Okay, so there's still an element of flinging.

In a recent development, much like Triband's previous efforts, What the Clash? is another wacky fun time that sees you competing – either solo or co-op – in numerous party games.

SpaceInvaders InfinityGene Evo (Taito Corporation).

According to recent reports, spaceInvaders InfinityGene Evo is, as the name suggests, an evolved version of the classic arcade shooter. Sporting the gameplay we all know and love, it throws in a few twists to help breathe new life into this familiar setup.

Katamari Damacy Rolling Live (Bandai Namco).

According to recent reports, everything you need to know is pretty much in the title. Katamari Damacy sees you rolling a stick ball that grows bigger as more and more items become stuck to it.

Pac-Man continues to be relevant in the gaming world and 256+ allows you to enjoy even more dot-munching action.

Industry observers note that drive Ahead! Carcade (Dodreams Fairytale Company).

Ever have the urge to drive recklessly? Well, here you can live out those bizarre fantasies with no real-world consequences! In Cardcade, the goal is to bonk your opponent in the head once. Yep, that's all it takes, which means it's not as simple as it sounds in practice.

Arkanoid vs Space Invaders+ (Taito Corporation).

Arkanoid vs Space Invaders+ combines the two classic games in one, tasking you with defending the Earth by deflecting bullets back at your foes.

Sources indicate that poncle's excellent Vampire Survivors is now available through Apple Arcade. If you're unfamiliar, it's a bullet heaven game where your character automatically flings a barrage of projectiles at your enemies, leaving you only worrying about walking away from any incoming danger.

Temple Run: Legends (Imangi Studios).

One of the most iconic mobile games is back, albeit with a slight twist. In Temple Run: Legends, there are levels to complete rather than the endless dash we're used to. On each, there are three stars to earn on the one-hundred-plus levels, so your swiping skills need to be on point.

Punch Kick Duck+ (Shaun Coleman).

Battle your way to the top of the tower where success lies in how good your timing is and whether or not you pick the right move.

Tomb of the Mask+ (Happymagenta).

Tomb of the Mask is an arcade action game that sees you exploring a tomb.

A Slight Chance of Sawblades+ (Yong Kian Chin).

In a strange and dangerous turn of events, it's raining saw blades. To survive the deadly storm, you must dodge, jump and backflip away from the tools dropping from the sky.

BEAST: Bio Exo Arena Suit Team (Oh BiBi).

Beast is a 3v3 shooter that sees you battling for the honour of your home planet. During each match, you can switch between pet and beast forms, making use of the different abilities and weapons each brings.

Everyone's favourite speed hedgehog comes to Apple Arcade to do battle with his old foe Eggman. Choosing one of six playable characters, you will dash, climb, and fly your way through each of the stages.

Recent findings suggest that as the name heavily suggests, Downwell sees you making your way down a well in search of treasure. To defend yourself, you are equipped with a pair of Gunboots to vanquish the threats that lurk within the well.

Taken on the role of James Bond in this top-down action adventure that draws inspiration from the last 60 years of the storied hero.

Junkworld is a tower defence where you take charge of the Scavenger clan and lead them to victory in a series of battle, making use of towers, special units and gadgets.

Ridiculous Fishing EX (Vlambeer).

A fishing game with a difference, Ridiculous Fishing EX sees you using guns, chainsaws, and even toasters as you head into the depths in search of a significant catch.

TMNT Splintered Fate (Viacom International).

Recent findings suggest that join everyone's favourite turtle quartet in this brand-new roguelike action game. Splinter has been captured and it's up to you to save him. You can play as any of the four Turtles, each with distinct abilities and powers alongside teaming up with three other players.

Time Locker is a shooter with a minimalist but colourful aesthetic. In it, you control the speed of time using your finger and must avoid obstacles and enemy attacks. The Apple Arcade version comes with fresh exclusive enemies.

Temple Run is one of mobile gaming's all-time classics. If, somehow, you're unfamiliar, it sees you running, jumping, and sliding through temples, collecting riches as you go.

According to recent reports, snake.io+ is a battle royale that sees you slithering around and eating pellets in a bid to become the last serpent standing. By cutting up other snakes, you can make them explode into pellets, which you'll want to gobble up to increase your size.

PPKP stands for Punch Punch Kick Punch, which gives you a rough idea of what to expect. You will attempt to save a city from deadly monsters by honing your martial arts skills so you can unleash a devastating combo to defeat them.

Getting Over It+(Bennett Foddy).

According to recent reports, navigate a world covered in random everyday objects by playing as a man in a pot wielding a hammer. It's as frustrating as it is odd, but ultimately rewarding if you manage to scale the mountain that lies ahead of you.

JellyCar Worlds (Walaber Entertainment).

Industry observers note that as the title suggests, in this driving/platforming action game, you play as a car made of bouncy jelly. With this in mind and armed with several abilities, the aim is simple. Navigate each level and find the exit.

In a recent development, motion Twins' excellent roguelike can now be enjoyed as part of your Apple Arcade subscription. It sees you playing as a failed experiment, setting off to explore wildly different biomes.

Jetpack Joyride 2 (Halfbrick Studios).

Barry Streakfries has returned. Once more, he will need to battle through the laboratory and attempt to put an end to the experiments being carried out there.

Subway Surfers Tag (Sybo Games).

In a recent development, the latest entry in the popular Subway Surfers series is an Apple Arcade exclusive. In Subway Surfers Tag, you will head to numerous city locations and skate, grind, and tag your way to a high score. The Guard will be there to make things more tricky though, so be ready to evade him.

According to recent reports, pick your favourite Sonic the Hedgehog character before running, jumping and dashing through plenty of levels. Alongside regular running levels, you will also face off against Eggman and Zac in special Boss Racing stages.

Alto's Adventure – Remastered (Snowman).

Alto's Adventure is a mobile classic that sees players embarking on a snowboarding adventure where they'll grind over rooftops and leap across perilous chasms. The remastered version includes upcoming challenges for players to tackle and several new set pieces.

Disney Melee Mania (Mighty Bear Games).

Industry observers note that disney Melee Mania is a MOBA that features a variety of characters from the franchise's many popular films. Each match lasts five minutes, making it great for playing on the go, and there are presently 12 Champions to choose from, including Buzz Lightyear and Wreck-It Ralph.

Oddmar sees the titular character embarking on a journey to prove himself worthy of a place in Valhalla. Along the way, he will collect magically imbued weapons and shields that will help him smite down his foes.

Get a blast of nostalgia with Galaga Wars+, which sees you taking control of the iconic spaceships and gunning down waves and waves of enemies.

Sources indicate that play as a cute bird who has always dreamed of flying. Run down hills to use them as jumps to soar through the air, if only for a moment.

The extremely popular Crossy Road is now available on Apple Arcade, allowing you to collect all the characters and the numerous stages as part of your subscription.

It has been revealed that the popular endless runner is now available on Apple Arcade. Fly through several levels using a bullet-powered jetpack as Barry Steakfries looks to put an end to a group of scientists who are up to no good.

Alto's Odyssey: The Lost City is the definitive version of the gorgeous endless runner. It features an all-new biome for players to explore alongside additional challenges to beat.

The classic slingshot action game returns with latest birds, pigs and challenges. There's also a brand new game mode to enjoy where players are tasked with stopping the Eagles from wreaking havoc on the island.

Recent findings suggest that leo's Fortune is a platformer where you will hunt down a fiend who rudely stole your gold. The game has received a lot of praise since it first launched, and now you can play it as part of your Apple Arcade subscription.

A retro-fueled underwater adventure where you can create your own soundtrack.

Compete with players from around the world in hyper-casual competitive mini-games or throw a Super Mega Mini Party with friends!

This is an action driving game where you'll be swerving around corners, collecting newly introduced powers, and shooting down choppers, all while zipping past bullets.

Bleak Sword is a dark fantasy action game tasking players to struggle across compact, cursed diorama battlefields.

The floor is lava, so you'd best stay off it any way you can.

Build your way to the top in this lighthearted, team-action brawler where anything can happen.

Creatures of the Deep+ (Infinite Dreams Inc).

Recent findings suggest that fancy going fishing? That's exactly what you can do in Creatures of the Deep, heading out in your little boat in search of an impressive catch. But be aware that disturbing shadows are lurking in the deep...

Oceanhorn 3 (Cornfox & Brothers).

According to recent reports, the third main instalment in the Zelda-like series takes place 1000 years after Oceanhorn 2, bringing you a completely upcoming adventure. You'll have to battle through the Shadow Sea, which doesn't sound like a pleasant place for a cruise.

SpongeBob: Patty Pursuit (Viacom).

Head down to Bikini Bottom for some side-scrolling action with everyone's favourite sponge. He's on a mission to find his missing fry cook station while Plankton joins him because his inventions have also been stolen.

Return to Monkey Island+ (Terrible Toybox).

This one's for the point-and-click adventure fans out there, particularly those who have previously enjoyed Ron Gilbert's work.

In this adventure, you'll form a team of Ubisoft's critters and use their special powers to vanquish your foes.

Tamagotchi Adventure Kingdom (Bandai Namco Entertainment).

In this colourful game, your goal is to restore the titular kingdom to its former glory by building and decorating your wilderness camp before inviting your Tamagotchi pals to enjoy it with you.

Industry observers note that from the creators of What the Golf? Comes What the Car?, a silly racing game where you can roll, jump, fly and even sneeze your way to the finish line. You play as a car, but rather than having wheels, you have a pair of legs. It's as fun as it is absurd.

Very Little Nightmares+ (Bandai Namco).

Very Little Nightmares is a puzzle adventure game where you are tasked with escaping The Nest, a giant maze littered with traps.

Enjoy the incredibly atmospheric Limbo as part of your Apple Arcade subscription. You play as a young boy who is looking for his sister and must traverse a deadly world to find her by solving puzzles and jumping over perilous gaps.

Old Man's Journey+ (Broken Rules).

Old Man's Journey+ is an emotional adventure that focuses on life's precious moments and aims that need to be changed.

Monument Valley 2+ (ustwo games).

The critically acclaimed adventure game Monument Valley 2 is now available through Apple Arcade. If you're unfamiliar, it sees players guiding a mother and her child through a world filled with magical architecture.

Gibbon: Beyond the Trees (Broken Rules).

The developers of Old Man's Journey and ELOH has returned with a game that looks to emulate the way gibbons swing from tree to tree. Meanwhile, the narrative tackles topics such as deforestation, poaching, and climate change.

Wylde Flowers is a life and farming sim, but with magical spells thrown in for good measure. You take on the role of Tara, who arrives on the island to help her grandma with the family farm. It promises to provide a whole adventure as you explore magical realms, beaches and forests.

Dandara: Trials of Fear+ (Raw Fury).

Sources indicate that raw Fury's Metroidvania Dandara: Trials of Fear can now be enjoyed as part of your Apple Arcade subscription. It sees you battling to save the world of Salt from an imminent collapse.

LEGO Star Wars: Castaways (Gameloft).

In Star Wars: Castaways, you will explore a mysterious planet that has been abandoned for a long time. Throughout the game, you will make new friends and battle against some imposing enemies.

In Monument Valley, you will manipulate impossible architecture and guide a silent princess through a stunningly beautiful world.

A modern twist on the trials and tribulations of the road to Oregon, this official successor to the global phenomenon will immerse players in exhilarating journeys ranging from the historically accurate to the completely wild.

A beautiful adventure game that explores how everyone can make a difference in the world even with the smallest of actions.

In a recent development, all of You is a cute, purely visual, accessible, family-friendly puzzle adventure with unique gameplay. Play and pause time in every part of the level to unveil the right path for the main character.

The Last Campfire is an adventure, a story of a lost ember trapped in a puzzling place, searching for meaning and a way home.

The ground starts shaking, light bulbs are breaking - and something rather unusual is happening right behind the walls of your very room. Equipped with nothing but wit and courage, you slowly descend into a world inhabited by avian folk and seemingly deadly furniture monsters.

Sequel to the classic adventure game Beneath a Steel Sky.

Beyond Blue takes you into the near future, where you’ll have the opportunity to explore the mysteries of our ocean through the eyes of Mirai, a deep-sea explorer and scientist.

It has been revealed that live the life of a Sasquatch and do regular, everyday Sasquatch stuff like: Sneak around campsites. Disguise yourself in human clothing.

FreeCell Solitaire: Card Game+ (MobilityWare).

Sources indicate that pretty much as it claims on the tin. FreeCell Solitaire lets you enjoy the classic card game in as straightforward a way as possible. No bells and whistles needed here.

Uno: Arcade Edition (Mattel163).

According to recent reports, if ruining long-standing friendships is your idea of fun, then you might want to give Uno: Arcade Edition a try. It's the classic card game we all love to get frustrated by with a few intriguing twists to the existing formula.

Crazy Eights: Card Games+ (MobilityWare).

It has been revealed that dip into some of your favourite tabletop card games with Crazy Eights. It has numerous modes to enjoy that mix up the rules, helping keep things fresh.

Texas Hold'em Poker: Pokerist+ (KamaGames).

No real surprises here, simply a way to play poker online, pitting your skills against other players to win big.

Sources indicate that localThunk's Balatro exploded in popularity when it released early in 2024. The simple concept of creating strong poker hands combined with deckbuilding, tactics and even some maths has led to it being viewed as one of the best games of the year. And now you can play it on your phone!

Monster Train+ (Good Shepherd Entertainment).

If you haven't played this excellent roguelike deckbuilder and happen to have an Apple Arcade subscription, you're now in luck. Monster Train sees you riding on the titular locomotive on a journey to restore a frozen hell to its former glory. Well, if hell is ever glorious, I suppose.

Blackjack by Mobility (Mobility Ware).

Sources indicate that this one's fairly self-explanatory, you can play the card game 21. You have unlimited chips too, so you can play against the dealer to your heart's content.

Pocket Card Jockey: Ride On (Game Freak).

In a recent development, pocket Card Jockey: Ride On is a game that combines solitaire and horse racing. The game previously released on Nintendo 3DS but is now available as part of your Apple Arcade subscription.

Gin Rummy Classic+ (MobilityWare).

Learn to play Gin Rummy using tutorials and perfect your skills against bots offline. The aim is simple: you want to create the best hand possible by picking up or drawing one card at a time.

Spider Solitaire: Card Game+ (MobilityWare).

Enjoy the classic card game Spider Solitaire as part of your Apple Arcade subscription.

Hearts: Card Game+ (MobilityWare).

Now you can enjoy the classic card game Hearts as part of your Apple Arcade subscription. You can test your skills against AI that adapts to your playstyle to make sure you stay on your toes.

Experience the classic card game with a plethora of beautiful deck designs, daily challenges and explore your competitive nature by trying to climb the leaderboards.

Sources indicate that the addictive game you’ve been playing on your computer for years now goes wherever you do. Whether you know it as Patience, Klondike, or just Solitaire, this popular game is one of the best games around.

Like its footwear namesake — Flipflop Solitaire is unrestrictive, creating a upcoming game for fans of spider, klondike and other traditional Solitaires.

Pusheen's Place (Electric Square).

Recent findings suggest that if the idea of adorable cat-like creatures appeals to you, then Pusheens is worth checking out. You'll gather a veritable army of them before popping them in their latest home, which you can also customise.

Unpacking is a Zen puzzler that sees you moving house several times over a period of time. It's entirely designed for relaxing, so you don't have to worry about timers, scores or any of that business. Just kick back and enjoy.

A bunch of evil monsters and villains need serving, and it's up to you to fulfil their orders.

The most famous and most popular endless runner is now available on Apple Arcade. Race along those tracks and grab coins to your heart's content without fear of any adverts of in-app purchases required.

It has been revealed that cleaning might not sound fun on the surface, but trust me, you'll love it in PowerWash Simulator. Armed with a powerful jet washer, you'll have to blast the muck off house, vehicles and other objects until they're spick and span. It's incredibly satisfying.

In a recent development, piffle+ sees you slinging adorable cats around levels to break all the blocks. It's a simple premise, but trickier to do in practice.

Suika Game is deceptively simple. All you have to do is get two of the same fruit to come into contact with one another so they merge to form a larger fruit, with the ultimate goal being to create a watermelon. It sounds straightforward and perhaps a little dull, but before you know it, an hour's passed and you'll be itching to make more watermelons.

Helix Jump tasks you with guiding your ball through a series of twisted towers using physics-based movement.

Sources indicate that there are few games as synonymous with mobile as Doodle Jump, and now this classic is available on Apple Arcade. The concept is simple, yet inherently compulsive. You can waste many hours on this one.

Talking Tom Blast Park (Outfit7).

Another entry in Outfit7's popular franchises, Talking Tom Blast Park sees the titular hero embarking on an adventure to stop Rakoonz.

Smash Hit+ sees you smash through an ethereal dimension in time with music. It promises to be a meditative experience despite the destruction you're leaving in your wake.

While Furista is a push as a pun, I'm happy for it count as a fan of felines. In this game, you adopt cats before matching your customers with them to make their visit to your cafe as fluffy and enjoyable as possible.

Industry observers note that collect and nurture fish so they become what they were always destined to be... Dragons! That's right. Zen Koi Pro+ is a relaxing experience that follows the Asian myth that koi can become dragons with enough care and attention.

Delicious – Miracle of Life+ (GameHouse).

It has been revealed that the popular casual management sim is now part of Apple Arcade. It follows Emily as she looks to progress her career while preparing to become a parent.

According to recent reports, if you've ever wanted to build your own farm, this might be the game for you. Farmside allows you to place plots, plant crops and harvest them. Beyond that, you can raise animals and spend time designing your farm's layout.

Sources indicate that 2017's App Store Game of the Year is now available through Apple Arcade. The aim is simple, you have to search for the titular hidden folks across numerous levels. There are over 300 in total with 32 hand-drawn areas to investigate.

Industry observers note that another of MobilityWare's card games is now available on Apple Arcade. This time you can play Spades as much as you'd like. The aim is to work with a partner to try and out-bid your opponents while trying to reach 250 points first.

Now you can enjoy the classic card game Hearts as part of your Apple Arcade subscription. You can test your skills against AI that adapts to your playstyle to make sure you stay on your toes.

Experience the classic card game with a plethora of beautiful deck designs, daily challenges and explore your competitive nature by trying to climb the leaderboards.

It has been revealed that the addictive game you’ve been playing on your computer for years now goes wherever you do. Whether you know it as Patience, Klondike, or just Solitaire, this popular game is one of the best games around.

Like its footwear namesake — Flipflop Solitaire is unrestrictive, creating a latest game for fans of spider, klondike and other traditional Solitaire games.

Blast off into outer space with an intergalactic indie rock band in the latest instalment in the popular Reigns series.

According to recent reports, bring your friends and see how far you can get in this endless spinning tower of arcade fun! Keep climbing as high as you can. Every run is different.

Would you believe me if I told you that there's a puzzler about folding paper that's incredibly beautiful? If you're an origami fan, most likely. But to anyone else, it'll be a pleasant surprise in Kami 2+.

In a recent development, block Blast is one of those simple yet endlessly engaging puzzlers. All you have to do is match blocks on an 8-by-8 grid and then enjoy them all exploding. However, it's never quite that simple, constantly asking you to think deeper than you might expect.

Art of Fauna: Cosy Puzzles+ (Klemens Strasser).

Industry observers note that if you love nature and puzzles, then Art of Fauna is perfect for you. It sees you essentially putting together some beautiful artwork, with each accompanied by some text about the depicted animal.

Water Sort Puzzle: Get Color+ (Tripledot Studios).

A colourful and relaxing puzzler that will keep you occupied for hours and hours.

Everyday Puzzles: Mini Games+ (Fanatee).

Sources indicate that it's a bunch of puzzles you can do every day, right? Pretty much! There is a mix of word puzzles and brain teasers for you to tackle each day to keep your mind strong.

According to recent reports, fancy yourself as an artist? Draw It gives you the opportunity to prove it, tasking you with sketching out a visual depiction of a word before the time runs out.

Perchang World (Perchang World).

Perchang is a physics-based puzzler that takes you through a series of colour environments. It's wacky fun that's all narrated by popular British comedian, James Acaster.

Sources indicate that flow Free is as simple as puzzlers can get. However, don't expect it to be easy. Connect up colours might sound straightforward, but it becomes very tricky over time.

It has been revealed that if you love pretty colours and solving puzzles, then I Love Hue Too+ is for you. It sees you rearranging mosaic tiles to make beautiful creations.

Let's Go Mightycat! (ponos corporation).

The Battle Cats now have a spin-off! Now you can fling them at blocky towers. It might sound straightforward, but making them all tumble to the ground isn't as easy as you might think.

Lost in Play+ (Snapbreak Games).

Lost in Play is a story about a brother and sister trying to find their way home. To do so, you will need to solve a series of puzzles alongside chatting with some whimsical creatures.

Words of Wonders: Search+ (Fugo Bilism).

Recent findings suggest that no great surprises here, Words of Wonder: Search+ is... a word search! That's right. It pretty much does exactly what it claims on the tin. So if hunting for a list of words is your jam, you're well catered to here.

Industry observers note that sumi Sumi: Matching Puzzle+ (Imagineer Co. Ltd).

Sumi Sumi is a puzzler that tasks you with matching popular characters from San-X together while enjoying all the beautiful animations that accompany doing so.

What do you get if you mix stickers with jigsaws? puffies. That's what! Designed to be a calming experience, it tasks you with open sticker packs before piecing together the various puzzles.

Put your word skills to the test with Zynga's Arcade edition of the popular puzzler Boggle.

Wheel of Fortune Daily (Frosty Pop).

If you're a fan of Wheel of Fortune and fans of daily puzzles, this game is exactly what you're looking. Each day, you will have to solve one, with plenty of variety promising to keep it fresh every time.

Enjoy some match-3 puzzling with a delightful cast of colourful characters.

Super Monsters Ate My Condo+ (PikPok).

Sources indicate that super Monsters Ate My Condo brings some whacky match-3 to the table. This new and updated version offers improved visuals but, thankfully, leaves the gameplay we all know and love untouched.

Recent findings suggest that the popular tile-matching puzzler comes to Apple Arcade. It sees you popping the titular Puyos across several different game modes.

Industry observers note that words in Progress sees you combining letters to create words. You can either find how long you can survive in Endless Mode or test your word crafting prowess against other players.

Cornsweeper promises to be a meditative puzzler where the aim is to avoid explosions going off. It draws heavy inspiration from Minesweeper, as you might have guessed by the name!

Puzzle & Dragons Story (GungHo Online Entertainment).

The popular series brings its blend of match-3 puzzling and RPG elements to Apple Arcade. By matching colours, you will battle your way through deadly dungeons while recruiting newly introduced companions to help you in the fight.

Knotwords is a word puzzler that brings together elements of Sudoku and crosswords.

Crossword Jam+ (PlaySimple Games).

Train your brain by engaging with a series of crossword-style games that see you looking to create words.

It has been revealed that om Nom is back in the third instalment in the popular puzzler series. The aim is to reunite Nibble Nom and Om Nom on each stage by engaging with the various mechanics that the game has to offer.

According to recent reports, finity. is a matching game with three simple rules to follow. But that doesn't mean it's going to be easy as you attempt to climb the leaderboards.

Nekograms is an adorable puzzler where the goal is to help every cat you encounter fall asleep. To do this, you have to move the felines and cushions around until they've found the perfect place to curl into a ball and nap.

Bold Moves+ is a puzzler where you match tiles to solve a series of word puzzles. It offers a mixture of daily and weekly events alongside plenty of levels to work through.

Disney SpellStruck (Artist Arcade).

Disney SpellStruck is a word puzzler that takes place on The Isles of Tiles. It tasks you with solving a bunch of crossword-like games with popular Disney and Pixar characters like Mickey Mouse, Stitch, and Tinkerbell.

Disney Getaway Blast+ (Gameloft).

It has been revealed that make your way through a series of matching puzzle games while working on your own tropical island. Along the way, you can get help from beloved Disney and Pixar characters, with each bringing special power-ups.

Doctor Who: An Unlikely Heist (Tilting: Point).

Sources indicate that if you enjoy the popular BBC sci-fi series and puzzlers, then Doctor Who: An Unlikely Heist might be for you. It sees you finding hidden objects and solving a series of puzzles.

According to recent reports, human: Fall Flat+ is now available on Apple Arcade. It's a jokey physics-based platformer that can be enjoyed on your own or with four pals.

Castle Crumble (Orbital Knight).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar spent a long time working on Grand Theft Auto 6, and it shows through the games many small details. There are tons of hidden easter eggs and secrets scattered across Leonida, and some of them connect to previous GTA titles.

According to recent reports, more specifically, there are a decent number that connect back to GTA 5. Have you ever wondered what happened to Michael’s boat? Who took the blame for the murder of Floyd and Debora?

Thanks to GTA 6, we now the answers to these questions, and there are many more connections to GTA 5 that you might not have discovered. Everything is connected after all.

It has been revealed that if you played GTA 5, odds are you spent a great deal of time exploring the map and going from town to town. It was quite a big map, but you wouldn’t have spent your entire time in the city, so you probably recognize Grapeseed and the Grand Senora Desert.

Grapeseed is a small town in the northern part of the GTA 5 map, with it residing in Blaine County. The Grand Senora Desert is a much larger area, but it also resides in Blaine County.

While exploring the many buildings that you can enter in GTA 6, you can wander into a few trailers, and some of them have postcards that link Leonida to Los Santos. You can find postcards specifically for Grapeseed and Grand Senora Desert.

Industry observers note that you get a lot of phone calls in GTA 5. Many missions start with you getting a call, and then proceeding to head to some location. Because of this, if you have played the story, you will have heard Michael’s ringtone quite a bit.

Well, if you feel so inclined, and want to stay true to the spirit of GTA 5, you can have Michael’s ringtone in GTA 6. All you need to do is go into your phone’s settings, choose the ringtone option, and then select the one called Wind Chimes.

This ringtone is exactly the same as Michael’s from GTA 5, giving you that classic GTA feeling from 13 years ago when you played the campaign for GTA 5.

Recent findings suggest that one of the best easter eggs in GTA 6 is that you can find Michael’s boat from GTA 5, and you don’t really need to go all that far. In fact, you have to stick rather close to home, because it is sitting right outside Jason’s house at the start of the game.

Michael ends up having his boat stolen in GTA 5, and you never learn what happens to it. Well, it somehow found its way to Leonida and ended up in Jason’s yard.

If you decide to climb up on the boat, you can see that a screen is still active on it. This screen reveals the shores of Los Santos from GTA 5, seemingly proving that this is indeed the same boat that was stolen from Michael all those years ago.

Sources indicate that do you remember Fabien? He teaches Michael how to do yoga in GTA 5, and is known for having some rather… suggestive yoga poses. Throughout GTA 5, you can perform yoga as Michael either at his house or at the peak of Mount Gordo.

According to recent reports, fabien has been doing well since the events of GTA 5, and you can see what he has been up to thanks to his article in one of the game’s magazines. This is also an easter egg that you can find outside of Jason’s house.

It has been revealed that go out onto the porch, and open the magazine that is on the table near the workout equipment. Flip through the pages, and you will find that Fabien has been doing well. He has been on an “epic pilgrimage of enlightenment.”.

It is a little ambiguous as to if the Mount Chiliad Mystery in GTA 5 was ever solved. While there is a means of seeing a UFO from it, it didn’t have a narrative conclusion, so it is debated on whether or not it was ever completed.

However, this mystery is mentioned in GTA 6, and it is on a vehicle. You can find an RV in Leonida that is covered in phrases like, “Don’t be fooled,” and “There’s no driving away.”.

According to recent reports, what connects this to Mount Chiliad is the eye symbol. It is the same eye symbol that is found at the top of the Mount Chiliad mural, making it seem like the mystery was never fully solved, or maybe that is just what Rockstar wants us to think.

There are some small nods to GTA 5 hidden throughout GTA 6, and one that is easy to overlook is a small book review for a novel sitting in Jason’s house. The book in question is titled Lethal By Design: A Liberty City Memoir, written by Tom Everett.

This book connects to the events of GTA 4 and Niko Bellic - a fan-favorite protagonist. With that being mentioned, one of the reviews is actually from a resident of Los Santos.

The review reads, “Illuminating, revelatory, heartbreaking, and pulse-quickening - and that’s before you’ve even finished the editor’s forward.” This review came from Alison Taylor from the Los Santos Book Review.

There is an obscure reference to GTA 5 in GTA 6, and it connects back to some of the promotional material for GTA 5. One of the trailers for GTA 5 featured a man with a newspaper on his desk.

If you are paying attention, you can see that the newspaper’s headline reads, “Aliens ate my prize [blank]. Of course, I have to bleep out the final word due to vulgarity, but it connected to GTA 4, and it also played into the insane satirical nature of GTA 5.

This same newspaper has returned, and it is in GTA 6. In a shack in the Grassrivers, you can spot the same newspaper sitting on a table. It is amazing that Rockstar remembered to bring back this strange newspaper.

Floyd and Debora Hebert were an unhappy couple living in Vespucci Beach in GTA 5. Their house is used as a safehouse by Trevor and their cousin Wade. However, they don’t survive the events of GTA 5, as Trevor murders them in a brutal off-screen killing that leaves him covered in blood.

It is never known exactly what happened after that event, but you can learn the truth of what transpired after the events of GTA 5 by listening to the radio in GTA 6.

If you listen to the crime thriller podcast channel on the radio, you will hear them talk about Floyd and Debora. It turns out that Wade got blamed for their deaths.

Latest Update: Scientists discover a fresh type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (981 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants.
  • The discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression.
  • Circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants. Researchers at the University of Sydney have discovered a subtype called "circadian depression," which appears to be closely connected to the body's internal biological clock.

The discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression. Nearly one-quarter of the participants in the study, which focused on people with severe, recurrent or persistent depression, revealed characteristics of this newly identified subtype.

Circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy. People with this form of depression tend to respond less favorably to common serotonin-based antidepressants. However, treatments that target the brain circuits involved in controlling circadian rhythms, including melatonin, melatonin-targeted antidepressants and light therapy, may offer more effective options.

Published in the British Journal of Psychiatry, the findings shed light on the genetic factors associated with this subtype and offer a possible explanation for why widely used medications such as SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) are less effective for some patients.

A Hidden Type of Depression Affecting Nearly One in Four Patients Studied.

Recent findings suggest that to investigate the biological differences between forms of depression, researchers examined information collected through the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Their analysis included clinical histories and genetic data from more than 10,000 people who had experienced depression.

In a recent development, the researchers identified nearly 25 percent (2,604 participants) as having circadian depression. Several recognizable patterns distinguished these individuals from other people with depression.

Recent findings suggest that those with the circadian subtype were more likely to experience seasonal changes in their depression, sleep for longer periods when depressed, and wake up feeling exhausted despite spending more time in bed. They were also more likely to be night owls, meaning they naturally preferred staying awake late and waking later in the day.

Industry observers note that the differences extended beyond sleep patterns. Depression often began earlier in life for these individuals, and their symptoms tended to be more severe (such as mania and higher levels of suicidal thoughts). Genetic analysis also revealed an increased predisposition to inflammatory and cardiovascular health problems, along with major neurodevelopmental disorders, including ADHD.

First author Dr. Emiliana Tonini from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Center said:.

"Our research has identified circadian depression as a upcoming subtype, affecting around a quarter of people in our study into those with severe, recurrent or persistent depression.

"Depression is not a uniform illness, and understanding the characteristics of different subtypes means that we can give people earlier access to treatments that will be most effective for them.".

Why Common Antidepressants May Be Less Effective.

One of the most important implications of the discovery involves how depression is treated.

Industry observers note that medications such as SSRIs and SNRIs (serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors) are generally among the first treatments offered to people diagnosed with depression. These drugs work by influencing chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood.

In a recent development, however, the researchers found that these medications tend to be less effective for people with circadian depression. Individuals with this subtype also experience more side effects, suggesting that conventional antidepressants may not be the best initial approach for everyone.

Because circadian depression is closely associated with the body's internal clock, therapies designed to influence that clock may be particularly useful. Light therapy, for example, uses controlled exposure to bright light to help regulate biological rhythms. Melatonin, a hormone involved in signaling when the body should prepare for sleep, and antidepressants that target melatonin pathways may also be relevant treatment options.

In a recent development, co-senior author Dr. Jacob Crouse from the Brain and Mind Center explained:.

"Because circadian depression is linked to people's internal body clock, treatments targeting the circadian rhythm, such as light therapy and melatonin, may be much more relevant, and clinicians should reach for these much earlier in people with this presentation.

"For those who find that antidepressants are not working for them, it is important to speak to your clinician for advice about your individual circumstances.".

A Upcoming Approach Could Improve Depression Treatment in Young People.

Recognizing circadian depression earlier could be especially vital for younger patients, who may otherwise spend valuable time trying medications that are less suited to their particular form of depression.

Professor Ian Hickie, Co-Director of the Brain and Mind Centre and a clinical psychiatrist, warned that failing to identify this subtype in young people can contribute to unsuccessful early treatments and unnecessary side effects.

Recent findings suggest that the findings highlight the importance of recognizing that depression is not a single, uniform condition. Different biological mechanisms may contribute to similar symptoms, meaning that treatments effective for one person may provide much less benefit to another.

By identifying patients whose depression is closely tied to circadian rhythms, clinicians may be able to offer more targeted treatments earlier rather than relying on the same initial medication approach for everyone.

"We really want young people to receive the most appropriate treatment early in their course of illness.

"Most young people will be offered SSRIs first up, but for at least a quarter there are better circadian-focused medical and behavioral options to help treat and manage their condition.".

Shopify Rebellion Black opened the North America Qualifier Playoffs with a 2-0 win over Xora Esports. The non-partner organisation is now one win from the playoffs that decide a guaranteed São Paulo Kickoff place.

The best-of-three Group Stage meeting with Xora began at 00:10 UTC on Saturday 21 November, opening Shopify Rebellion Black’s VCT Americas Kickoff: North America 2027 campaign.

The result counts for more because Shopify Rebellion is now outside Riot’s partnership system. The organisation was one of the Americas sides that mentioned it had not been chosen for the 2027-2028 partnership programme, Sheep Esports reported. Cloud9, ENVY, M80, FlyQuest and LYON were also on that list. Riot now has eight partner teams in each of its four regions.

The Swiss Stage runs from 20 to 22 November 2026. Every match is best of three. Two wins send a team through to the playoffs, and two losses knock it out. The eight teams left after the Swiss phase move into a double-elimination bracket played over six competition days, with the playoffs set for 1 to 6 December. The event is listed as an online, A-Tier Riot Games qualifier for 16 teams.

Recent findings suggest that shopify Rebellion Black’s next opponents are Oafs, who also won their opening match 2-0, against QoR. Both teams are therefore one win from the playoffs. Oafs already have a record against Xora. They knocked them out of the Qualifier 1 bracket on 8 November with a 2-1 win. Xora had still reached the Qualifier Playoffs by finishing joint third in the 512-team North America Qualifier 1.

Recent findings suggest that across 83 rated matches, Shopify Rebellion Black hold a 59-24 record. Before this event their most recent series was a 2-3 defeat to 2GAME Esports at the VCL Americas Last Chance Qualifier 2026. Earlier in that event they had beaten 2GAME Esports 2-1 and Contra 2-0.

According to recent reports, the organisation’s second line-up had a harder start. Shopify Rebellion Gold lost 0-2 to Maryville University. Several of the other organisations left out of the partnership programme won their first matches. Cloud9 beat counterfeit 2-0, Team Envy beat Yellow Dragon Gaming 2-0 and FlyQuest edged Masterclass 2-1. Elsewhere, Winthrop University beat SaD Esports 2-0 and YFP Gaming beat Wildcard 2-1.

Recent findings suggest that the prize for coming through the bracket is a place in São Paulo. Riot will stage the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in Brazil. Its eight Partner Teams get direct entry. Non-partner teams can win four places: one guaranteed slot each for North America, Brazil and Latin America, plus one for the Americas Last Chance Qualifier. For a non-partner side, a later run to Masters would be worth a fixed US$200,000 and a place at Champions US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. The regional Kickoff events are due to start on 14 January 2027 and run until 7 February 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A few weeks ago, my brother sent me a photo with zero context. He was at our parents’ house, helping them pack up for a cross-country move, when he found something unusual: a heavy metal box with a latch.

It took me a second to dust off the cobwebs in that corner of my mind, but once I did, I recognised the box as the promotional material Nintendo sent me back in 1998 to celebrate the original release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

I asked my bro what was inside the box and a few moments later he replied with another picture. The box was empty.

It has been revealed that I can’t think of anything more depressing than an empty treasure chest. All the anticipation leading to… crushing disappointment. Anyone who ever slogged through the Phoenix Cave in Final Fantasy VI knows the feeling.

Sources indicate that this chest originally housed a pre-launch, gold N64 cart of Ocarina of Time. It was Nintendo’s not-so-subtle message that this game was a treasure. A bit on the nose, but the zeitgeist of an entire generation of gamers has certainly proven them right. OoT is a treasure.

Sources indicate that in this case, I can at least take solace knowing that I'm the one who emptied the chest and thoroughly enjoyed its golden treasure. The empty box is evidence of that.

My brother’s timing was impeccable — bordering on eerie — unearthing the box less than a week before the Switch 2 remake rolled out.

In a recent development, like many of you, my son (let's call him Tim) and I were eagerly awaiting the OoT remake. He hadn’t played the original, but is an avid Zelda fan, particularly the modern titles. I knew I’d love the Remake, but I was a bit nervous that he would have a different reaction. He’s a member of this Breath of the Wild, open-world generation, after all. Would the old-school Zelda formula appeal to his generation, or would it die with mine?

As they say, sometimes one man’s treasure is another man’s trash.

Recent findings suggest that my love for Zelda, and desire to pass it down to my son, parallels the experience my father had with his four boys. Dad loved to work with his hands and my brothers and I were always enlisted in projects: everything from clearing the land, felling trees, reroofing the house, building an addition, repainting, and working on a long series of rundown cars. He made sure we received hands-on working experience.

In a recent development, right around the time I received the Zelda Treasure Chest, my dad began restoring classic Ford Mustangs in his garage. I had already moved out, but my youngest brother ( the one who found the chest) was there to be Dad’s understudy. Together they restored two beautiful Mustangs, allowing my dad to share his love for mechanical craft and manual labour.

Sharing an old classic is one thing, but actually passing down a passion depends on how well the original holds up to modern sensibilities.

It has been revealed that A restored car regains its iconic look, but it will also retain the old feel, complete with stiff brakes and crank windows. After all, restoring something doesn’t place it in a state opposite to its nature. A 1967 Mustang GT Fastback is a 1967 Mustang GT Fastback only if it looks, sounds, and feels like a 1967 Mustang GT Fastback, for better or worse.

Industry observers note that media remakes and remasters are often criticised for following this type of approach. Shot-for-shot remakes come across as unnecessary cash grabs (looking at you Disney) while complete reimaginings seem to either spectacularly succeed (Dune, Casino Royale, Metroid Zero Mission) or fail (Planet of the Apes 2001, Secret of Mana, Quantum Leap).

Like my old man, Nintendo’s philosophy seems closer to restoration than reimagining. Star Fox and Super Mario RPG are recent examples, with the slightly more ambitious Link’s Awakening preceding them by a few years. There are many others.

Sources indicate that in each case, the spirit of the original is preserved while a few quality-of-life improvements are added. And of course, each old classic receives a newly introduced coat of paint.

According to recent reports, by taking this approach, Nintendo has been careful to avoid the pitfalls that so many media companies encounter when updating beloved products. Their roster of remakes have largely avoided any 'Han shot first' controversies. Thank goodness.

A philosophy of preserving the original’s frame, while souping up the engine, allows old and upcoming players to enjoy the gaming experience without fighting retro clunkiness.

So, what does Tim think of Ocarina of Time?

He loves it, of course! And it’s been immensely satisfying to see him enjoy it. Confirmation bias can be a wonderful thing.

In a recent development, the wife and I have a ritual of playing Zelda games together, so we’re playing it in short, infrequent bursts. I’m not complaining, as it’s allowed me to savour the experience. Tim, on the other hand, is powering through it at a much faster pace. He also spectates while my wife and I play. We always aim for a 100% run, so Tim takes notes on all of the heart pieces and bag upgrades he missed.

I’m just excited to see my son enjoying a game I grew up with. My dad passed on his love for mechanical craft to his boys, and I’m sharing my passion for sidequests with mine.

It’s been a good month. It began with a nostalgic relic and a bit of disappointment (grr, I still can’t find that gold cart), but also included a timeless masterpiece that’s been successfully passed to the next generation.

Sources indicate that 30 years ago my dad shared the muscle cars from his youth. This year I got to share a classic Zelda adventure from mine.

I wonder what treasure my boy will pass on to his kids in 30 years' time.

Have you successfully passed a favourite game down to the next generation? Was it the original, or a remake that added modern improvements? Share your stories in the comments below.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Upgrade, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

It has been revealed that since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

It has been revealed that the Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

Recent findings suggest that the Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside latest Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the substantial day.

#166541. Latest gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good
